name: free_conv_plates_and_sphere
title: Free convection from plates and a sphere: Nusselt-number correlations (function library)
summary: Five EES FUNCTIONs returning the Nusselt number of natural convection from an isothermal surface: Churchill-Chu for a vertical plate (smooth laminar-to-turbulent transition, valid on the whole Rayleigh-number range), McAdams, VDI Heat Atlas and Rohsenow-Hartnett-Cho for a horizontal plate (each with the buoyancy-assisted hot-plate form and the cold-plate form of its lower surface, the McAdams and VDI ones being non-smooth switches between the laminar and turbulent branches) and Churchill for a sphere. Pr and Gr are arguments, so the calling model passes them; the heat-transfer coefficient follows from h = Nu*k/L_c and is left to the caller.

authors: S. W. Churchill and H. H. S. Chu (Churchill-Chu vertical-plate correlation)
V. D. I., VDI Heat Atlas, with K. Stewartson 1958 and E. U. Schluender 1987 (VDI horizontal-plate correlations)
W. Rohsenow, J. Hartnett and Y. Cho (Rohsenow-Hartnett-Cho horizontal-plate correlations)
S. W. Churchill, as presented in E. U. Schluender (1987) (Churchill sphere correlation)
origin.notes: ht 1.2.0, commit 85e0ee6 (2025-12-07), file ht/conv_free_immersed.py, MIT license, Copyright (C) 2016 Caleb Bell. The scientific basis of each correlation is the original paper or book cited in its function comment block (Churchill & Chu 1975, Bergman et al. 6E; McAdams, Heat Transmission; VDI Heat Atlas 2nd ed. 2010, Stewartson 1958, Schluender 1987; Rohsenow, Hartnett & Cho 1998). The same module as CSL-0092 (free_conv_cylinders), whose Popiel-Churchill function repeats the vertical-plate correlation of this model. Translation published under the CoolSolve_Library MIT license (decision D3).

verification.reference: doctest values of ht 1.2.0 ht/conv_free_immersed.py (case A: 10 published values - the vertical-plate and sphere correlations, the four Nu_horizontal_plate_McAdams values including its two lower-surface (cold plate) ones and its low-Prandtl set, and the hot-plate and lower-surface value of the VDI and of the Rohsenow correlation) and additional values computed with the same ht functions in a throw-away virtualenv (cases B and C: the laminar and the turbulent branches of the horizontal-plate correlations, both faces); 26 output values in total
verification.notes: compare_solution.py: 26 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); largest relative deviation 3.4e-13 (Nu_horizontal_plate_McAdams_A_lowPr_cold), i.e. round-off in the double-precision evaluation only.
